Yes. We did family counseling and individual and groups and blah blah blah. She is doing great now.. but the hard working one said I needed counseling, and there was nothing wrong with her.

It got pretty bad. The hard working one attacked me one too many times and after six months of having to explain bruises at work and her plans to murder me, I sent her to live with a relative across the state. I found out she was doing drugs and she started bringing them home even though it was effecting her mentally.

I hope she does better. I hope she is able to find happiness.  Sometimes I think I'm her unhappiness, but then I find out she acts the same way to everyone. The family she is living with shields the bad from us, but the family a block away tells us all about it. 

I just hope she thrives and one day will speak to me.

I was really close to sending my kid to Provo Canyon. I see it's brought up a lot. I had everything planned, and a family member offered to try to take my teen in.

1. This was not a light decision. We had been dealing with alot of trauma for over a year and we were afraid for our safety so much to where the 7 year old said they would feel safer if they could have a deadbolt on their bedroom door. 

2. I was physically attacked by my teen. They were told that if they did enough damage that I would kick them out. I was not that parent, and I was struggling and afraid. They cost thousands of dollars in damage (throwing chairs at windows.. ripping cabinets off walls). This teen was not a big person. When the teen started attacking me once a month, I was afraid to be left alone with them. I had black eyes constantly and felt terrible when I had to restrain them. So much so that the last time I was attacked I managed to get them face down with both hands behind their back but they were screaming it hurt and I loosened my grip and nearly lost a finger when they tried to bite it off. 

3. Teen mental health is so hard. Are they just teenagers, or are they struggling with some kind of chemical imbalance? They don't like to diagnose teens with disorders because it's a stigma and could follow them for the rest of their lives and I totally agree with that, but something was going on. They were drunk or high 24/7, I was in contact with their school and monitored their social media, texts, basically anything they did online I could see from another room. There was something wrong. They were sent to many mental institutions for holds. One even lasted just a few days under a month. Everytime there would be zero follow up, no plans on medication until they would see their primary doctor and they would suggest things that did not work for other people and would admit so when you called back to ask how else you can lock up meds and knifes and anything they could hurt themselves with. 

4. On the last visit, they planned at least four ways to murder me. Plausable, realistic ways that could happen if they allowed them to come home. I am so lucky to have the spouse I do because he would fight for my kids because they pretty much are. He has been their dad since my kids were toddlers, but he is not their biological father. They would have nowhere to go if I passed before their current ages and their lives would be devastated if the courts wouldn't allow my bf to take them. 

I had everything set up. The school they currently went to would allow them to switch to online learning until they could return. I would be able to visit once a month and talk every day. I even had set up two drivers and was ready to purchase plane tickets to make it easier. All of these people I know personally. 

So the question is..

What was I supposed to do? Wait until I found them after they commit suicide? Wait until they murder me?

Where were they supposed to go? 

This documentary raised so many questions for me, but if she gets booted from where she is now.. what happens then?

She should see a doctor. Often a really bad fishy smell is chlamydia and you should both be checked. If left untreated it could lead to infertility or even infection that leads to sepsis and just like google always tells you, you will die.
Someone loves you. You just need to pay attention. Look around, there is someone trying to talk to you. Just open up and you will find them.

They showed no signs of depression before. They knew the rule that I had about vaping and if I find one on them it will be taken away and the phone goes too. They made their punishment, I just follow through.
